rules.source: Irish Data Protection Act 2018, Section 29 — fixes the national age of digital consent (GDPR Article 8) at 16; a child under Section 29 is defined as under 18 for other child-specific protections in the Act. https://caseguard.com/articles/a-new-legal-framework-for-data-protection-in-ireland/

Irish Data Protection Act 2018 — it is a specific criminal offence for a company or corporate body to process a child's personal data for the purposes of direct marketing, profiling, or micro-targeting; the DPC's "Children Front and Centre" guidance sets out 14 child-specific data-processing principles. https://www.dacbeachcroft.com/en/What-we-think/In-the-Spotlight-Processing-Childrens-Personal-Data-in-Ireland-and-beyond

Irish Data Protection Act 2018 — provides a specific, strengthened right to erasure for children with respect to personal data collected when they were offered an information-society service, going beyond the general GDPR Article 17 right. https://www.dataprotection.ie/sites/default/files/uploads/2023-04/DPC_ChildrensData_ParentalConsent.pdf
